questions.prompt: The period of \(f(x)=6\cos(\frac{2 x}{5} + 2)\) is \(k\pi\). Find \(k\). ______

questions.prompt: The period of \(f(x)=\tan^{2}(\frac{5 x}{4})\) is \(k\pi\). Find \(k\). ______

questions.explanation: First find the two periods: \(5 \pi\) and \(2 \pi\). The period of a sum is \(\dfrac{\text{LCM of numerators}}{\text{HCF of denominators}}\). Writing the periods as fractions of \(\pi\): \(5\) and \(2\) give \(10\pi\). So the period is \(10 \pi\).

questions.prompt: The period of \(f(x)=\cos^{2}(6 x)\) is \(k\pi\). Find \(k\). ______
questions.explanation: An even power of sin or cos removes the minus sign, so the period is halved to \(\dfrac{\pi}{|b|}\). (\(\tan^n\) has period \(\dfrac{\pi}{|b|}\) for every \(n\).) Here \(b=6\), so the period is \(\frac{\pi}{6}\).

questions.prompt: The period of \(f(x)=\cos^{2}(\frac{3 x}{2})\) is \(k\pi\). Find \(k\). ______
questions.explanation: An even power of sin or cos removes the minus sign, so the period is halved to \(\dfrac{\pi}{|b|}\). (\(\tan^n\) has period \(\dfrac{\pi}{|b|}\) for every \(n\).) Here \(b=\frac{3}{2}\), so the period is \(\frac{2 \pi}{3}\).

questions.prompt: The period of \(f(x)=\cos(3 x) + \tan(\frac{3 x}{4})\) is \(k\pi\). Find \(k\). ______
questions.explanation: First find the two periods: \(\frac{2 \pi}{3}\) and \(\frac{4 \pi}{3}\). The period of a sum is \(\dfrac{\text{LCM of numerators}}{\text{HCF of denominators}}\). Writing the periods as fractions of \(\pi\): \(\frac{2}{3}\) and \(\frac{4}{3}\) give \(\frac{4}{3}\pi\). So the period is \(\frac{4 \pi}{3}\).

questions.prompt: The voltage in a circuit is \(V=230\sin(20160t)^\circ\), \(t\) in seconds. Find the frequency in hertz (cycles per second). ______
questions.explanation: Period \(=\dfrac1{56}\) s, so frequency \(=56\) Hz.

questions.prompt: The period of \(f(x)=\sin^{3}(\frac{x}{4})\) is \(k\pi\). Find \(k\). ______
questions.explanation: An odd power of sin or cos keeps its sign changes, so the period stays \(\dfrac{2\pi}{|b|}\). Here \(b=\frac{1}{4}\), so the period is \(8 \pi\).

questions.prompt: The minimum value of \(y=2\sin(\frac{x}{2} - 2) + 1\) is ______
questions.explanation: For \(y=a+b\,\sin(\cdots)\) the maximum is \(a+|b|\) and the minimum is \(a-|b|\). Here \(a=1\), \(|b|=2\), so \(M=3\) and \(m=-1\). (The sign of \(b\) and the inside of the bracket do not change the extreme values.)

questions.prompt: Number of zeros of \(y=\tan(3 x)\) for \(0<x\le\pi\): ______
questions.explanation: The zeros of \(y=\tan(3 x)\) are at \(x=\dfrac{n\pi}{3}\). Counting those with \(0<x\le\pi\) gives 3.

questions.prompt: The maximum value of \(y=10\cos x + 24\sin x\) is ______
questions.explanation: For \(y=a\cos x+b\sin x\), the maximum value is \(\sqrt{a^2+b^2}\) (and the minimum is \(-\sqrt{a^2+b^2}\)). Here \(\sqrt{100+576}=26\).

questions.prompt: The period of \(f(x)=\frac{1}{2}\sec(\frac{7 x}{2} + 5)\) is \(k\pi\). Find \(k\). ______
questions.explanation: For \(y=\sec(bx+c)\) the period is \(\dfrac{2 \pi}{|b|}\). Here \(b=\frac{7}{2}\), so the period is \(\frac{4 \pi}{7}\). The coefficient in front and the shift inside do not change the period.

questions.prompt: The height of a buoy above the sea bed is modelled by \(d(t)=15+3\cos\!\left(\dfrac{2\pi t}{6}\right)\), \(t\) in hours. Find the least value. ______

questions.prompt: Voltage (in V) of \(V=170\sin(18000t)^\circ\) at \(t=\frac{1}{120}\) s: ______
questions.explanation: The angle is \(18000\times\frac{1}{120}=150^\circ\). So \(V=170\sin150^\circ=85\) V.

questions.prompt: The period of \(f(x)=3\cot(4 x)\) is \(k\pi\). Find \(k\). ______
questions.explanation: The period of \(\cot(bx+c)\) is \(\dfrac{\pi}{|b|}\) (tan and cot repeat every \(\pi\), not \(2\pi\)). Here \(b=4\), so the period is \(\frac{\pi}{4}\).

questions.prompt: The period of \(f(x)=\sin(\frac{x}{3}) + \cos(\frac{x}{3})\) is \(k\pi\). Find \(k\). ______
questions.explanation: First find the two periods: \(6 \pi\) and \(6 \pi\). The period of a sum is \(\dfrac{\text{LCM of numerators}}{\text{HCF of denominators}}\). Writing the periods as fractions of \(\pi\): \(6\) and \(6\) give \(6\pi\). So the period is \(6 \pi\).

questions.prompt: The maximum value of \(y=4\sin(\frac{x}{2} - 2) - 1\) is ______
questions.explanation: For \(y=a+b\,\sin(\cdots)\) the maximum is \(a+|b|\) and the minimum is \(a-|b|\). Here \(a=-1\), \(|b|=4\), so \(M=3\) and \(m=-5\). (The sign of \(b\) and the inside of the bracket do not change the extreme values.)

questions.prompt: The maximum value of \(y=2\sin(\frac{x}{2}) + 2\) is ______
questions.explanation: For \(y=a+b\,\sin(\cdots)\) the maximum is \(a+|b|\) and the minimum is \(a-|b|\). Here \(a=2\), \(|b|=2\), so \(M=4\) and \(m=0\). (The sign of \(b\) and the inside of the bracket do not change the extreme values.)

questions.prompt: The period of \(f(x)=\sin^{2}(\frac{2 x}{5})\) is \(k\pi\). Find \(k\). ______
questions.explanation: An even power of sin or cos removes the minus sign, so the period is halved to \(\dfrac{\pi}{|b|}\). (\(\tan^n\) has period \(\dfrac{\pi}{|b|}\) for every \(n\).) Here \(b=\frac{2}{5}\), so the period is \(\frac{5 \pi}{2}\).

questions.prompt: The period of \(f(x)=\tan(\frac{x}{2}) + \cos(\frac{5 x}{2})\) is \(k\pi\). Find \(k\). ______
questions.explanation: First find the two periods: \(2 \pi\) and \(\frac{4 \pi}{5}\). The period of a sum is \(\dfrac{\text{LCM of numerators}}{\text{HCF of denominators}}\). Writing the periods as fractions of \(\pi\): \(2\) and \(\frac{4}{5}\) give \(4\pi\). So the period is \(4 \pi\).

questions.prompt: A Ferris wheel of radius \(5\) m has its lowest point \(3\) m above the ground and makes one revolution in \(120\) s. A rider boards at the lowest point. Height (in m) after \(80\) s? ______
questions.explanation: A rider who starts at the lowest point follows \(h(t)=8-5\cos\!\left(\dfrac{2\pi t}{120}\right)\) (centre height \(=\text{radius}+\text{platform}=5+3=8\) m). At \(t=80\) s the angle is \(2\pi\cdot\frac{2}{3}\), \(\cos=- \frac{1}{2}\), so \(h=\frac{21}{2}\) m.

questions.prompt: The minimum value of \(y=4\cos(x) + 1\) is ______
questions.explanation: For \(y=a+b\,\cos(\cdots)\) the maximum is \(a+|b|\) and the minimum is \(a-|b|\). Here \(a=1\), \(|b|=4\), so \(M=5\) and \(m=-3\). (The sign of \(b\) and the inside of the bracket do not change the extreme values.)

questions.prompt: The period of \(y=-3\sin\left(\frac{1}{2}x\right) + 3\) is \(k\pi\). Find \(k\). ______
questions.explanation: Period \(=\dfrac{2\pi}{|b|}=4 \pi\).

questions.prompt: The maximum value of \(y=4\cos x + 6\sin x\) is ______
questions.explanation: For \(y=a\cos x+b\sin x\), the maximum value is \(\sqrt{a^2+b^2}\) (and the minimum is \(-\sqrt{a^2+b^2}\)). Here \(\sqrt{16+36}=2 \sqrt{13}\).

questions.prompt: The period of \(y=3\cos\left(4x\right) + 1\) is \(k\pi\). Find \(k\). ______
questions.explanation: Period \(=\dfrac{2\pi}{|b|}=\frac{\pi}{2}\).

questions.prompt: The minimum value of \(y=7\sin^2x + 1\cos^2x\) is ______
questions.explanation: Use \(\sin^2x+\cos^2x=1\): the expression is a weighted average of \(7\) and \(1\) with weights between \(0\) and \(1\), so it lies between them. Maximum \(=7\), minimum \(=1\).

questions.prompt: The temperature in a room is modelled by \(d(t)=12+5\cos\!\left(\dfrac{2\pi t}{24}\right)\), \(t\) in hours. How many hours pass between two successive maxima? ______
questions.explanation: The time between successive maxima is one period \(=\dfrac{2\pi}{2\pi/24}=24\) hours.

questions.prompt: The maximum value of \(y=3\sin(x) - 3\) is ______

questions.prompt: The smallest positive \(x\) where \(y=-3\sin(\frac{x}{2}) + 2\) reaches its minimum is \(k\pi\). Find \(k\). ______
questions.explanation: The minimum needs \(\sin(\frac{1}{2}x)=1\) (because \(b<0\)). The smallest positive angle with that value is \(\frac{\pi}{2}\), so \(x=\dfrac{\frac{\pi}{2}}{\frac{1}{2}}=\pi\).

questions.prompt: If \(\cos\theta=- \frac{40}{41}\) and \(\theta\) is in the second quadrant, find \(\tan\theta\). ______
questions.explanation: Use \(\sin^2\theta+\cos^2\theta=1\) to find the missing ratio, then fix its sign from the quadrant (ASTC). Here \(\sin\theta=\frac{9}{41}\), \(\cos\theta=- \frac{40}{41}\), so \(\tan\theta=- \frac{9}{40}\).

questions.prompt: The period of \(f(x)=\cos^{2}(4 x)\) is \(k\pi\). Find \(k\). ______
questions.explanation: An even power of sin or cos removes the minus sign, so the period is halved to \(\dfrac{\pi}{|b|}\). (\(\tan^n\) has period \(\dfrac{\pi}{|b|}\) for every \(n\).) Here \(b=4\), so the period is \(\frac{\pi}{4}\).

questions.prompt: The smallest positive \(x\) where \(y=2\sin(x)\) reaches its minimum is \(k\pi\). Find \(k\). ______
questions.explanation: The minimum needs \(\sin(1x)=-1\) (because \(b>0\)). The smallest positive angle with that value is \(\frac{3 \pi}{2}\), so \(x=\dfrac{\frac{3 \pi}{2}}{1}=\frac{3 \pi}{2}\).

questions.prompt: Of the six trigonometric functions, ______ and cot are the two whose range is all real numbers (name one of them).
questions.explanation: tan and cot take every real value.

questions.prompt: If \(\sin\theta=\frac{7}{25}\) and \(\theta\) is in the first quadrant, find \(\cos\theta\). ______
questions.explanation: Use \(\sin^2\theta+\cos^2\theta=1\) to find the missing ratio, then fix its sign from the quadrant (ASTC). Here \(\sin\theta=\frac{7}{25}\), \(\cos\theta=\frac{24}{25}\), so \(\cos\theta=\frac{24}{25}\).

questions.prompt: The minimum value of \(y=6\cos(x) + 4\) is ______
questions.explanation: For \(y=a+b\,\cos(\cdots)\) the maximum is \(a+|b|\) and the minimum is \(a-|b|\). Here \(a=4\), \(|b|=6\), so \(M=10\) and \(m=-2\). (The sign of \(b\) and the inside of the bracket do not change the extreme values.)

questions.prompt: The period of \(f(x)=\sin(3 x)\) is \(k\pi\). Find \(k\). ______

questions.explanation: Midline \(=\dfrac{\max+\min}{2}=\dfrac{18+(-2)}{2}=8\).

questions.prompt: The period of \(f(x)=\sin(kx)\) is \(\frac{3 \pi}{2}\) (with \(k>0\)). Find \(k\). ______

questions.prompt: The period of \(f(x)=\cos(\frac{3 x}{4}) + \tan(\frac{x}{2})\) is \(k\pi\). Find \(k\). ______

questions.prompt: The period of \(f(x)=\left|\sin(6 x)\right|\) is \(k\pi\). Find \(k\). ______
questions.explanation: Taking the absolute value folds the negative half of the wave upwards, so the pattern repeats after half a period: \(\dfrac{\pi}{|b|}\). Here \(b=6\), so the period is \(\frac{\pi}{6}\).
